steps.name: Look back over its history
steps.instruction: Nothing to do on the device. ZMM looks back over what it has reported since it joined, and proposes the maker's attributes that changed in step with something already known (a target temperature, say). The longer the device has been in use, the more this finds.

steps.name: Values I know
steps.instruction: Nothing to do on the device. Enter values you know it has now, from its own app, its display or its manual, as name: number pairs separated by commas (a pasted JSON object works too). ZMM finds the maker's attribute holding each, with its scale, and says where more than one fits.

steps.name: Change an on/off setting on the device
steps.instruction: Name one setting, then change it on the device itself (its manual says how, e.g. holding a button to turn the LED off). Change only that one.

steps.name: Set a number on the device
steps.instruction: For a setting that holds a number (a temperature, a percentage, a time): name it, then set it on the device itself to a value you choose and enter that value here. Change only that one.

inputs.name: new_value
inputs.label: The value you set it to

steps.name: Let ZMM flip one (visible)
steps.instruction: For a setting the device will not show you how to change: name it, then let ZMM flip one candidate at a time while you watch the device. Each is put back as soon as you answer, or after 60 s.

inputs.name: to_label
inputs.label: What the flip should show (e.g. Off)

steps.name: Let ZMM flip one (behaviour)
steps.instruction: For a setting that changes how the device behaves rather than what it shows (e.g. open-window detection): name it, then let ZMM flip one candidate and hold it for up to 15 minutes while you provoke the behaviour (open the window by the valve). Answer when the device reacts, or that it did not. It is put back when you answer.

inputs.name: to_label
inputs.label: What the flip should show (e.g. Off)
